text:
jamie: Weird alert — warm-pool GPU nodes failing to finish ephemeral keystore decrypt in eu-south-1 after a regional firewall segmentation change. Nodes stuck in Provisioning.

noor: saw that on dashboards. Join success went from ~98% to ~55% at 09:07 UTC. Keystore proxy returns 403 on /decrypt. Not a KMS key issue (decrypt failures are auth-related).

diego: ssh'd into a failed node: outbound TCP to keystore LB on 443 is RST from the new firewall. The new segmentation was supposed to restrict tenant peering; looks like our warm-pool subnets are now in a different zone.

ops-bot: [CANARY] 1797665432: eu-south-1 canary results: 6/10 joins succeeded, 4/10 failed (keystore auth). Logs: /var/log/infra/canary-eu-south-1-2026-03-21.log

jamie: immediate remediation options: (A) open narrowly-scoped egress to keystore LB CIDR and redeploy warm pool, (B) route keystore traffic via privatelink (longer), or (C) deploy a regional keystore mirror inside the new zone that accepts the new zone's connections.

noor: favour (A) as an emergency patch. We should make the allow as narrow as possible (single IP /32 or service tag). Also add a short lived audit entry so security has traceability.

diego: I've run a staging test with an NSG rule allowing the exact LB IP and port 443. Join rate recovered to 96% within 5m. Command used (staging):
```
az network nsg rule update --resource-group rg-prod --nsg-name warm-pool-nsg --name allow-keystore-outbound --priority 210 --access Allow --protocol Tcp --direction Outbound --destination-address-prefixes 10.56.12.8/32 --destination-port-ranges 443
```

security-team: tagging in. We need an exception record with justification, blast radius, and removal ETA. Also confirm audit retention impact if we backfill logs for failed joins.

jamie: agreed. Drafting exception INF-7901 with these fields: reason, CIDR allowed, window (<=18h), mitigation, and owner. Will LL @security-team for sign-off.

noor: note on costs: if we backfill join/audit logs for the 40% failed nodes we saw earlier, estimate ~60GB extra/day -> roughly $1.5k/week. Not huge but call it out in the ticket.

diego: let's add automation to remove the rule after 12h if join rate stays >95% for a 20m rolling window. I can push a CloudWatch/Monitor alert to trigger NSG rollback.

ops-bot: [ACTION] 1797665448: Proposed change queued: create NSG rule allow-keystore-eu-south-1 (10.56.12.8/32:443) with 12h TTL. Approve? (reply yes/no)

jamie: yes — approve. Executing now.

ops-bot: [AUTOMATION] 1797665456: NSG rule allow-keystore-eu-south-1 created on warm-pool-nsg (prod-eu-south-1). Canaries re-run.

noor: canary re-run shows 94% join success in 7m. Keystore decrypt 403 errors dropped to baseline. Monitors green but keep an eye for audit-shipper spikes.

security-team: exception logged INF-7901. Security approves conditional on these controls: 1) rule TTL <= 24h, 2) documented rollback plan, 3) audit entry with backfill cap (7d) unless compliance requires otherwise. Please attach canary logs.

jamie: done. attaching canary logs and cost note. Next steps: diego to implement auto-rollback, noor to monitor joins + audit backfill plan, jamie to start privatelink design doc for the keystore (ETA 2w).

diego: starting on rollback automation now. Also will prototype a regional keystore mirror to reduce cross-zone reliance (spike in work but may be faster than privatelink in some regions).

noor: FYI ops finance — if we end up doing a one-time full backfill instead of cap, numbers could be 3x our current estimate. Flagging for budget hold.

ops-bot: [AUTOMATION] 1797665460: Canaries stable. Monitoring subscription created: infra/monitors/keystore-eu-south-1. Auto-rollback scheduled at 12h unless override.

jamie: thanks everyone. Closing this temporary emergency thread once INF-7901 lands in security queue and auto-rollback is confirmed. If anything pops, escalate to oncall.
